correctness.rationale: The object is precisely the induced-edge count in a uniform k-subset; its probability mass is the exact integer histogram divided by binom(n,k), and the mean is k(k-1)/n. A complete induction shows every unlabeled tree of order at most ten arises from leaf augmentation, and canonical center-root codes distinguish tree isomorphism types. The included Python-standard-library certificate exhausts all 1,1,1,2,3,6,11,23,47,106 tree types, enumerates every subset, verifies every histogram sum, all sufficient and nonsufficient one-depth choices through eight, every one-depth collision count for nine, all 21 two-depth choices for nine, and the ten-tree pair collision. The domain is finite, so an exhaustive, complete generator plus exact comparisons is a proof; no infinite extension is claimed.

originality.rationale: The novelty candidate is the complete minimum-size collection of fixed-cardinality sampled-edge-count distributions that separates every unlabeled tree of each order four through nine. Tittmann–Averbouch–Makowsky (2008/2011) prove a stronger all-cardinalities distinction through nine and a ten-vertex full-data collision, but do not state the precise one-depth versus two-depth threshold or enumerate all five optimal depth pairs for nine. Liao–Hou (2013/2014) treat structural information in the full polynomial and Q-unique graph families. A separate current published-findings search did not identify the cardinality-slice experimental-design theorem. The earlier full-polynomial results and ten-vertex obstruction are explicitly not claimed as new. The literature review cannot prove absolute uniqueness and an unindexed table remains a risk.
residual_risks: A prior unindexed computational table could already give optimal cardinality-specific coefficients for trees through nine; searched sources did not resolve that possibility.
The 1993 induced-subgraphs-in-trees article was not accessible in full; its abstract concerns asymptotic ensemble distributions and no decisive exact finite inverse comparison was available.
The ecology publication was consulted for sampling motivation at abstract level only, not for a whole-document noncoverage claim.

value.rationale: The natural experiment-design question for ecological network censuses asks how many different sampled-taxon counts must be used to identify all tree topologies when taxon labels and link identities cannot be retained. A sample expectation is completely topology-blind, yet a single entire distribution identifies all 23 eight-vertex trees; at nine taxa exactly two distinct depths are necessary and five optimal choices are classified. This is a sharp information-compression threshold at the boundary before the already-known ten-vertex complete-information loss, not an arbitrary parameter slice or mere recomputation of a known full-polynomial uniqueness result. The claim is limited to idealized exact laws and does not assert that practical field sampling achieves the information bound.
